---
title: "Contribute"
description: "How to propose a workflow, a prompt, a skill or any other contribution."
---

Anyone can propose content. Every contribution is reviewed before it is published.

## Two ways to contribute

- **With Git:** fork the [repository](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site), add a file in `workflows/`, `prompts/`, `skills/`, `agent-configs/`, `model-checks/`, `reviews/` or `failures/`, and open a pull request.
- **Without Git:** [open an issue](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new/choose) and fill in the form for your kind of contribution.

A maintainer reads every proposal. If something is missing, the issue gets the label **needs-info** and a comment that says what. When it is complete, it gets the label **ready**: it is then turned into a page and a pull request within a day, and published when the pull request is merged.

## What every contribution needs

Every contribution (a workflow, a prompt, a skill, an agent config, a model check, a review or a failure) is one page of the site, written as a `.qmd` file that starts with this header. Copy it into a new file and fill it in:

````markdown
---
title: "Short, task-based title"
description: "One sentence: what it does."
# categories: literature, proposals, code,
#   analysis, writing, review
categories: [literature]
phase: "Literature"
model: "Model name and version"
tool: "Interface or tool"
tested: 2026-10-31
qflag: L1
time-saved: "3 h -> 40 min (measured)"  # workflows only
# date of publication
date: 2026-10-31
author:
  - name: "First Last"   # orcid is optional
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
    affiliations:
      - name: "Institute"
---
````

A failure needs only `title`, `description`, `date` and `author`.

Leave out the `catalog` field. When a contribution is published it gets a catalogue number automatically: the letter of its type and the next free number, for example **AI W003** for a workflow or **AI P002** for a prompt. The number never changes, so you can use it to cite or mention the contribution.

## Sections for each type

After the header, use these sections, in this order:

- **Workflow**, in `workflows/name.qmd`: Goal · What you need · Steps · How to check the result · Where it fails.
- **Prompt**, in `prompts/name.qmd`: Prompt (exactly as used) · Example (real input and output) · Known limits.
- **Skill**, in `skills/name/index.qmd`, with `SKILL.md` and any scripts in the same folder. The page shows the file itself with a ```` ```{.markdown include="SKILL.md"} ```` block and lists it under `resources` so it can be downloaded: What it does · SKILL.md · How to check the result · Where it fails.
- **Agent config**, in `agent-configs/name.qmd`: The file to copy (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`) · How to check the result · Where it fails.
- **Model check**, in `model-checks/name.qmd`: Task · Prompt · Expected answer · Results (model, date, answer, pass or fail).
- **Review**, in `reviews/name.qmd`: Paper reviewed · Model, date and review prompt · Points checked and confirmed · Points checked and rejected · Points not yet checked · Authors' reply.
- **Failure**, in `failures/name.qmd`: What happens · How to catch it · How to prevent it · Cases.

Every contribution ends with a **History** section: one dated line per change, starting with the first version, for example `- 2026-10-31: first version (L1), First Last.`

Reviews follow the extra [ground rules](reviews/index.qmd#ground-rules): only published papers, every confirmed point checked by a scientist in the field, and a right of reply for the authors.

## Credit and citation

Every contributed page shows its authors and ends with a **How to cite** box, with a ready-made reference and BibTeX entry built from the title, the authors, the date and the page address.

Contributions are published under the site licences: text under CC BY 4.0, code under MIT.

## Review criteria

- A colleague in the same field can follow the contribution and reuse it.
- Prompts are given exactly as used.
- *How to check the result* is concrete, not "verify the output".
- Nothing confidential or under embargo is included.

A contribution enters at **L1** when the author has tested it on a real case. It moves to **L2** when someone else reproduces it. Untested contributions are welcome too: they are published as **L0** drafts.

## Updating a contribution

A contribution keeps its catalogue number for life. Update it when:

- you tested it again, with another model or on another date;
- you fixed or clarified a step, or improved a prompt;
- you found a new case where it fails;
- you reproduced it (L1 to L2) or checked it across models or dates (L3).

If the method itself changes, propose a new contribution instead. It gets a new number and says *Supersedes AI W002* at the top, and the old page links to it.

**With Git:** edit the existing file and open a pull request.

- Leave `catalog` and `date` as they are. A pull request that changes a catalogue number is rejected automatically.
- Update `model`, `tested` and `qflag`, and add `date-modified` with the date of the update. It appears under the title as *Modified*.
- Add a line to the History section: the date, what changed, who made the change and with which model.

**Without Git:** [open an Update issue](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=8-update.yml) with the catalogue number and what changed.

Whoever reproduces a contribution (L2) or rewrites a substantial part of it is added to its authors. Smaller changes are credited in the History. When you cite a contribution that has been updated, give the date of the version you used: the catalogue number and the address stay the same.
